result.summary:
Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (36 layers, 32 heads with GQA 4:1, MLP width 12288). 14 parts passed the screen. Most were found from the weights first and many are large enough to transplant.

ARITHMETIC (two_digit_addition; control = copy the first operand):
- L23 heads [4,7,30,31]: addition drop .414. Picked by OV digit-copy score: digit embedding mapped to the same digit's unembedding, 5.7/5.2/4.7 for heads 30/7/4 against under 1 for every non-digit token class.
- The same group grown to 8 heads: drop .463. Two of the five random parts reached .26 and .22, so the margin is smaller.
- L23 MLP reader clusters at 256 / 512 / 1024 / 2048 units: drops .433 / .438 / .448 / .436, all random parts at most .02. Built purely from weights: an SVD of the L23 digit-head OV outputs on digit tokens gives a 12-dim subspace, and I ranked MLP units by how much of their gate and up rows lies in it. Subtraction cross-talk grows with size (.07 at 256, .14 at 2048, limit .145).

NUMBER EMISSION (recall_first_number; control = recall the first word of a word list):
- L34 number-writer MLP clusters at 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 / 1024 units: drops .53 / .54 / .60 / .58 / .47, control near 0, all random parts at most .005. Picked by the cosine between each down_proj column and the digit unembedding direction; the top units' logit lens is exactly the digits 0–9.
- L34 GQA group 3 (heads 12–15, shared v_proj): drop .237, control -.074, random parts at most .019.

LIST INDEXING:
- L22 MLP, 20 units (attribution): python_list_index drop .211, everything else about 0, random parts at most .003. Similar sets exist at L20 and L21, so indexing is spread over L20–22.

FACTS:
- Whole block L30: facts .353, others at most .111. It passed, but random single blocks reached .298, so the margin is thin. Facts is spread out within the L26 and L30 MLPs.

STRONG BUT UNSCREENABLE (several of my skills drop together):
- L23 GQA groups 1+7: addition .643, subtraction .56, months .33.
- The L24 MLP is the broad arithmetic layer: addition .44, subtraction .44.
- L35 GQA group 6 (effect sits in h25+h26) cuts math .21 and number recall .50 together.

NEAR MISSES / NEGATIVE RESULTS:
- object_color is carried by L26 attention but caps at .136.
- Multilingual is entangled with facts in the L31–34 MLPs (best .141).
- Translation sets failed held-out.
- Late relation-OV heads (successor, plural, bracket, capitalisation, antonym) were inert.
- Token-class writer clusters other than digits were inert.
- The reader recipe failed outside L23: L14, L22, L24, L26, L29, L34 and L35 head subspaces gave inert readers.

LESSONS:
- (a) Recipe for large units: find heads with a specific OV map, take the SVD subspace of their outputs, then rank the same layer's MLP units by how much they read from it. It scales to 2048 units while staying selective, but only where those heads feed a computing MLP (L23 arithmetic), not where they write the answer directly.
- (b) Whole GQA groups are natural head units, and bisecting a layer's attention by GQA group localises effects cheaply.
- (c) Don't define overlapping skills: they block screens of shared parts.
- (d) Attribution scans keep at most 20 units per layer and missed the L23 heads; weight-first did better on this model.

One new part passed this run: a 64-unit L22 MLP cluster for python_list_index. Catalog id: mlp_python_list_indexing_l22_mlp_grown_64-unit_clust_qwen3vl_8b_L22_k64_001. I used 4 of 41 screens; the other three failed.

**The passed part**
- Built by seed growth from 13 L22 seeds: the attribution top units 5178/4629/10532/6365/6380 plus the earlier passed 20-unit set. Units were added by summed gate/up/down weight cosine to the seeds.
- Ablating it drops python_list_index by .173. Every other skill and control moves at most .015, and random same-size parts move it at most .004.
- Growing it further made it weaker (96 units: .123, 128: .10 to .14, 256: .126). The 64 units look like the core, and the added units partly work against it.

**Same recipe elsewhere, all below the bar**
- en_fr translation at L32, grown from the earlier 20-unit near-miss: .078 at 64 units, .093 at 128, .067 at 512. Clean on other skills, but too weak.
- en_fr at L29/L31; list indexing at L23/L18/L34; times_table at L10/L14; code at L22; multilingual at L33/L35: at most .08.
- L28 MLP clusters aligned with month, colour or code output tokens: no effect (at most .007).

**Failed screens**
- **object_color:** L26 attention groups 0,1,4,5,6 dropped it .149, with no other skill above .035. Random L26 parts reached .133 and the held-out check failed.
- **facts, L28 block:** dropped facts .20, but random blocks matched it and the held-out check failed.
- **facts, top half of the L31 MLP by gate·up·down norm:** dropped facts .234 cleanly, but random halves of L31 reached .15 to .27. The whole L31 block cuts facts .47 but also multilingual (.20) and general_text (.15). L31 attention alone does almost nothing (.012), so the effect is spread across the MLP.

**Head groups with little or no effect**
- list indexing: L20 groups 1,2,7 (.011), L21 group 4 (.040)
- multilingual: L20/L22 groups (best .078)
- times_table: L14/L22/L23/L26 groups
- math and code: L35 groups 0-3 and 4,5,7, L33 groups 0-3
- Blocks L25 and L26 hit facts and addition together, so they aren't selective.

**For later runs**
- Seed growth works best when one attribution seed dominates, as 5178 does at L22. Stop growing once the drop peaks, which here was at 64 to 128 units.
- On this model, facts and colour are spread over whole layers, so random same-size parts match them.
- Retire the overlapping arithmetic skills (addition, subtraction, times_table) to free skill slots.
